verdict.root_cause: cartservice cannot start because REDIS_ADDR was pointed at redis-cart on port 6380, a non-default Redis port nothing appears to be accepting on. An automated environment edit set that override ~2 minutes before onset and, unlike five earlier set-then-revert cycles, it was still in the 'set' state at onset [tr_c51f05a773e8]. From 01:01 cartservice loops: startup, connect attempt to redis-cart:6380, 15-35s hang, unhandled exception from the cart-store initialize path, termination, restart — five cycles, with no request-handling lines at all [tr_c1b519477518]. Because the process never binds its gRPC server, callers' GetCart calls fail instantly client-side: checkoutservice PlaceOrder traces after 01:00:58 collapse from ~50 spans/~25ms to 3-5 spans aborting under 3ms, the erroring span being a client-side GetCart with no cartservice server or HGET child [tr_69e3db2d6829]; the frontend's only error trace is the same two-span GetCart shape [tr_1e503ae35abb]. The frontend and checkoutservice alerts are propagation toward the caller.
verdict.reasoning: Change, log and trace evidence converge. The change log gives a concrete wrong value with matching timing [tr_c51f05a773e8]; the logs show that exact endpoint dialed at startup and the exception killing the process before it serves [tr_c1b519477518]; the traces show the consequence an absent server predicts and a degraded one does not — client-side-only GetCart errors in ~0.5ms with no server child [tr_69e3db2d6829, tr_1e503ae35abb]. Not bad_deploy: the image at onset was the pre-hotfix reference and nothing changed it within the half hour before onset [tr_c51f05a773e8]. Not dependency_latency: callers get immediate errors, not waits [tr_69e3db2d6829]. The crash loop is how the wrong value expresses itself; the mechanism is a value naming an endpoint that does not serve. checkoutservice is excluded as origin — no change records at all [tr_cb79b3844139], no error lines, requests still arriving and truncating upstream of payment [tr_43e6ac2688ad]. A restart alone would re-enter the loop; there is no cartservice deploy to roll back.
open_questions: No one probed redis-cart: whether it listens on 6379 rather than 6380 is inferred from the port being non-default and connects hanging rather than being refused [tr_c1b519477518]. If redis-cart genuinely serves 6380 and is down, blame shifts to it.
Why this cycle's override did not self-revert after ~8 minutes as the prior five did [tr_c51f05a773e8] — late, wedged, or disabled automation changes whether manual action is needed.

checkoutservice's aggregate error ratio fell to about a third of baseline [tr_ff5a457b6dc3] while its traces show PlaceOrder failing outright [tr_69e3db2d6829]; that contradiction, plus no frontend trace coverage at 01:02:30 [tr_1e503ae35abb], leaves true blast radius unquantified.

alternatives.root_cause: The redis-cart instance is itself down or unreachable, and cartservice's startup crash is the symptom of an absent backing store rather than a wrong port value.
alternatives.why_not: An automated edit introduced a non-default port two minutes before onset where no override existed, and the same override was applied and reverted five times prior [tr_c51f05a773e8]; the wrong value explains onset timing without needing an independent Redis outage.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice restarts are an infrastructure-level crash loop (resource limit or probe kill) that happens to interrupt Redis initialization.
alternatives.why_not: Every termination is preceded by an explicit unhandled exception from the Redis connection path with startup stack frames, not a silent kill [tr_c1b519477518]; no OOM or restart counters were queried, but the application-level cause is recorded.

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring cartservice's environment to the pre-01:00:02 state (no REDIS_ADDR override, i.e. the default redis-cart:6379 target) and recreating the container should end the crash loop. Observable in cart-service logs: the startup line should name the default port, the connect attempt should succeed instead of hanging 15-35s and throwing the unhandled cart-store-initialize ApplicationException, the repeating startup/terminate cycles ([tr_c1b519477518]) should stop, and GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync request-received lines should reappear within one or two request intervals. Observable in traces: checkoutservice PlaceOrder traces should return from 3-5 spans aborting in under 3ms to ~40-55 spans around 25ms with a cartservice-side GetCart server span and its HGET child present ([tr_69e3db2d6829]), and the frontend two-span erroring GetCart shape should cease. Note that cartservice's own error-ratio series is empty in both incident and baseline windows ([tr_066fbe8032b6]), so confirmation must come from logs and traces, not from that metric.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, after the revert and recreate, cart-service logs still show connect attempts hanging then failing with the same cart-store-initialize exception — now against the default port. That would mean redis-cart genuinely serves 6380 (or is down entirely), the port being non-default was a red herring inferred only from connects hanging rather than being refused ([tr_c1b519477518]), and blame shifts to redis-cart. Also falsified in a weaker sense if the crash loop stops and then resumes: platform-automation re-applies this same override on a recurring cycle and five prior set/revert pairs are recorded ([tr_c51f05a773e8]); if the override reappears, this action is a temporary patch and the real fix is in the automation, which is outside what this system may do.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is inverted — redis-cart actually listening on 6380 and unhealthy — this revert points cartservice at a port nothing serves and keeps it crash-looping, having also discarded the current container and burned the ~2-3 minutes it takes to observe another five cycles. If platform-automation is mid-cycle rather than wedged, a manual revert races the automation's own revert and may leave the recorded config and the live config disagreeing, making the next automated set/revert pair harder to reason about. The recreate itself drops any in-flight GetCart/AddItem calls. Because no one has probed redis-cart, this proposal is acting on an inference, not a measurement; a redis-cart port probe before executing would cost little and remove the main failure mode.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice's container is replaced: frontend (GetCart, AddItem, EmptyCart on the product and cart pages) and checkoutservice (GetCart and EmptyCart inside PlaceOrder) see connection resets for the duration of the recreate — though both are already failing on this hop, so the practical degradation is small. loadgenerator-driven checkout and cart traffic is the visible surface. redis-cart sees cart traffic move from port 6380 to the default port. No other service in the incident's radius (adservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, currencyservice, paymentservice, shippingservice, emailservice, accountingservice) is touched; the post-01:00:58 traces show requests aborting before those hops are reached.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend and checkoutservice plus the load generator within seconds of each other describe a user-facing failure that cannot be dismissed, and no open incident covers it. The shared downstream dependencies of both seeds are the natural first place to look, but nothing in the alerts points to a specific fault class yet.
